utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber would prefer not to deal with any procedural matters at this moment but to do, if there's a need to do that, later today, and to start first with the continuation of the examination of the witness. Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Witness 4. I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony yesterday. Mr. Kearney will now continue to examine you. Mr. Kearney, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness number 4, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yesterday we took -- when we took a break, we were just about ready to discuss your sister M. And before we discuss her, I'd like to ask you, or I want to clarify something from yesterday. You mentioned the name of one of the men who repeatedly came to your home yesterday as Toger, or Togeri. Just for the sake of the record, I want to ask you, does that name have a meaning in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer and speak in the microphone because the interpreters could not hear your answer? Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it seems that the microphone of the witness is not turned on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your microphone seems not to be on. Let's verify. Because the witness was speaking loud enough now but ... Could you please repeat your answer again? It could well be, since I heard him so well, that actually that I receive what he said on the English channel. Let's try it again. Could you again give an answer to the question whether Togeri means anything special in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of any special meaning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I take it that you're fully aware that if there's a need to go into private session, that we should do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I am aware. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Yes, I'll ask Madam Registrar for a small redaction, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, can you please, again, tell us what happened in relation to your sister M?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was night, I think it was around 10.30 p.m., when Toger with some other soldiers came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When this incident happened, were you inside your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where were you inside your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the room where we usually slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When these men came to your home -- when Toger and these men came to your home, were you sleeping or were you awake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At some point during the incident, did you wake up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know what it was, Witness 4, that woke you up that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening, when they came, they broke down the door, the entry door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is that the events that woke you up that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Tell us what happened, please, after the entry door was broken down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night, after they broke the door open, Toger and some other soldiers entered the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How many soldiers were with Togeri on this evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four or five, but I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us how both Toger and these men were dressed, if you could?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toger was wearing the clothes of the special unit, as always.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were these the clothes that were black in colour that you described yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How about the other men? What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other men, among whom Xhevat Islami, he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Besides Xhevat Islami, did you recognise any of the other men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How was Xhevat Islami dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had camouflage military clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: On those camouflage military clothes did he -- was there any insignia visible to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in position to see and pay attention because there was no electricity at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was there any light inside the home at all during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not ordinary light, but when they came they had flashlights.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The camouflage-style clothing that Mr. Islami was wearing, had you ever seen that kind of clothing before in your village or in the area around your village during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the clothes that the military used to wear in the past, as I described them yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you say "the military," are you referring to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During this visit to your home, were the men wearing anything on their faces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Xhevat Islami was wearing a mask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And how about Togeri?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't have a mask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. How can you say who it was if this person was wearing a mask?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say who it was because before the war, he came to our house on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: These men that came into your home on the evening in question, were they armed or un-armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Xhevat had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What type?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it exactly. It was a rifle or another type of weapon, but it was a kind of big weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How about Togeri? Was he armed that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say yes, because he was always armed. Whenever I saw him he was armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What happened after these men came into your home this evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When these men came at our house that evening, Xhevat Islami said that he had come to our house in the name of Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you know who that was at that time, who Ramush Haradinaj was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had only heard of his name, Ramush, but I had never seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you say that Xhevat said he came in the name of Ramush Haradinaj, what do you mean by that? Were those his exact words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, I am Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you believe him when he said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we knew who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During this incident did Togeri, himself, say anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toger went to the other room where my sister was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is that something you could see or could you hear? Please tell us how you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him leaving our room and heading towards the room where my sister was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: While he was in your presence before he went to your sister's room, did you hear him say anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He just went and took my sister with him and then went outside at the entry door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did any of the men tell you or any members of your family why they were taking your sister?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. That's a compound question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you split it up, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd be happy to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did any of the men tell you why they were taking your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of anyone saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were you able to see your sister as she was being taken from -- taken from your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw her for a while when they took her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What was she wearing when they took her away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Black clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please describe them for us, if you can?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was wearing black trousers, a black sweater, and a leather jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was she wearing anything on her feet that you know of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you say you don't know that, do you know if she was or was not wearing shoes or you just don't know at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the shoes that she usually wore, we found them in the house the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was she allowed to -- or did she take any personal belongings with her the night that she was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I really don't remember. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After your sister was taken from the home that night, did you ever see her alive again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When was the next time you heard any news of her or her whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this event, four days later, a person came and he told us who it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: What do you mean, "a person came"? Who was it, and what did this person say, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person was called Can Mala and he was from Bardhaniq village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He came, asked us how we were doing, and we just said, We're fine. And then he asked us, Did you lose anything? And we said, Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What was it that you told him you had lost?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had lost our sister four days ago. He asked us what she was wearing. We described what she was wearing, and then he said, Yes, that's her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can you spell for us, please, the first name of this man from Bardhaniq who came to visit you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can Mala.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The first name begins with the letter C; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he go by any other names that you know of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You indicate that he was from the village of Bardhaniq; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How far is that village from Ratis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I would say 5 or 6 kilometres far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After you had this conversation with this gentleman, did you go with him toward Bardhaniq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was another young man with me, and we went to pick up the body of my sister by a horse cart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you went to -- when you went with this man towards Bardhaniq, did you eventually see the body of your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where was she?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a kind of road that divides Zabel and Bardhaniq, and it was on the foot of the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How far off this road was your sister's body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 4 or 5 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you eventually show this location to investigators from the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the Court's permission, I'd like to show this witness 65 ter Exhibit 1189, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. Of course, I haven't seen that exhibit. If there are no persons visible on it, I think it could be -- there's no need to have it under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Actually, this may need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, "may." Would you please tell us now so that we know whether we can show it to the public, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I believe it does need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number P25, under seal, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, is this a photograph of the location of your sister's body when you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it already on the witness's screen? Because it's not yet on the English screen. Witness, do you have any picture on your screen at this moment or not yet? No. Then we'll have to wait until --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Loading pictures just takes some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm informed this is on the English channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we're on the B/C/S channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, on the English channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has the witness -- do you see the picture on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you now see the picture on your screen, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is that the location where you found your sister's body on the day in question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you went to that location from this man -- with this man from Bardhaniq, when you arrived was there anyone else there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Who, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some persons whom I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain what they were, but I think they were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And were any of them wearing any distinctive clothing that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw only one person that was wearing camouflage trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were these individuals men or women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot ascertain the exact number but I think there were six or seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How close were they to the body of your sister when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Referring to these persons that we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, 10 to 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In the photograph P25 that you have before you there is pictured what appears to be foliage, trees, bushes. I want to ask you, if the body of your sister was -- was covered with such material or was it visible --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection; leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied, but at the same time you are making a distinction, Mr. Kearney, between being covered or visible which is not a clear distinction. So, therefore, I suggest that you reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's a point well taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness, was the body of your sister visible from the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was 4 or 5 metres away into the forest and we couldn't see it from the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us the condition of your sister's body when you first saw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I first saw her she was covered with a blanket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know if she was clothed or unclothed under the blanket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the waist up she was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you first saw the body --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, could you please seek clarification, because the question was whether she was clothed or unclothed and then the witness said, "From the waist up she was not," which leaves it open whether she was not unclothed or whether she was not clothed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, can you explain your last answer. Did she have any clothes on her body in the upper portion of her body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw her she had knife cuts on her upper part and in the throat, on the throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In one moment we'll get to the injuries you saw on her, but for the time being I want to ask you specifically about her clothing. You mentioned earlier that under the blanket she was not clothed. Please explain that for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the lower part she was dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did she have any clothes on the upper half of her body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw her, on the shoulder and on the throat I don't think she had clothes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you see any of her clothing items near the body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had the -- her leather jacket was thrown a little away from her body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How far from her body was the jacket when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe 1 or 2 metres. Not far from the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What was the condition of the jacket itself when you saw it, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was bullet-ridden and full of knife cuts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you notice anything else about the jacket that was significant to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was open, unbuttoned, and I saw the holes of the bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you notice any signs of trauma to the body of your sister itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw knife cuts on the arm, on the throat, and -- and I saw a bullet-hole on the earlobe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Besides the knife cuts you just told us about on the arm, did you see anyone -- anything -- strike that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At some point, Witness 4, did you count the number of perforations in the jacket that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't have time to count them because I felt very sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was there any indication that you saw, when you first discovered the body of your sister, that told you how long she had been in that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't know that, but she was missing for four days from that night that I described.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know if there were shoes on your sister's body at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When we found her body, no, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: She did not have shoes on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She didn't have any shoes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you see any shoes in the vicinity -- vicinity of the body when you found her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What did you do, if anything, please, with your sister's body after you discovered it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We carried her and brought her home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And how was that accomplished?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We carried her through the cart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon? Did you take the jacket with you or did you do anything with the jacket?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When we buried her, we left the jacket at home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: No, before, when you carried her, her body, on the cart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We brought the jacket with us along with the body and then we left it at home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During the transportation of your sister, did you notice any blood on her body or her clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the throat and where she had the injuries, we saw blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you transported the body from that location back home, or when you began to transport it, were the men you had described earlier still there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did any of them help you in the process of transporting the body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person who came and told us and Can Mala. The person - correction - was called Can Mala.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Besides him, did any of the other men you described, including the one wearing the partial camouflage, help you with the body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What did you do with the body, Witness 4, after you brought it back home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We brought the body home and kept it at home for that night, and on the next day we went and informed the uncles to come and bury her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, bury her at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How long after you retrieved the body of your sister did you bury her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We buried her after five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is that five days from when she was taken from your home or five days after you discovered her in the forest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the fifth day after we found her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During that -- those five days before the burial, what did you do to the body, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember to have done anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where was it that your sister was buried?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was buried near our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At some point during the investigation, did you show an ICTY investigator where you had -- where you had buried your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness another exhibit. This is 65 ter 1026, 1026, and again this should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It may be shown to the witness. Madam Registrar, would that be P26?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: You're correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Marked for identification for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, is there an image now on your screen that you can see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is that the location on your land where you buried your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At some point during the investigation of this case, did you give ICTY investigators permission to exhume your sister's body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was that done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know when that exhumation took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think two years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: From the time your sister was buried in that location to the time her body was exhumed, was the grave disturbed in any way that you know of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which grave do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The grave of sister M.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see anything. But I know that the grave was not surrounded by any fence or anything, and it was easy for any animal to have access to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But did you see anything happen to the grave between when the burial took place and when the exhumation took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there when the exhumation took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After the exhumation took place, were you ever shown personal artefacts of your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Then we -- they asked us what clothes she had on, and then we gave them the clothes we found on her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you -- when you removed your sister's body from the forest, did you notice any personal items on it that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a blanket but a blanket that didn't belong to our house. Someone else must have thrown it on her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know who that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, I now want to bring you back for a moment to 1998, if I may, to the time when your sister M was taken from your home, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you if your -- what happened -- or where did you live after your sister M was taken from the home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We lived in two rooms. The sisters lived in the other part of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After your sister M was taken from your home, did you continue to stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We continued to live for five days. After we buried the sister, we didn't live there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were scared to continue living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to stay with the uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What was it that you were afraid of, Witness 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were afraid that what had happened to our sisters might also happen to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During the investigation of this case were you at some point shown a photo-array by investigators from the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you know when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first time when we went to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, you were interviewed in 2004, 2005, and 2006. On which one of those occasions was it that you viewed this photo-array?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain but I think it was in 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please tell us how that process worked, if you could?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were answering the questions asked of us, a person showed us an album with photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You said, "When we were answering the questions asked of us ..." You were together with somebody when answering these questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was with my brother.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please, can you continue on that maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you were shown these photographs by the investigator, were you with your brother at that time or were you by yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection. I think we need to be extremely careful at this point in terms of the manner in which any questions proceed. I really think this is a point in time when the witness should have no potential leading or suggestive question asked of him concerning this particular event in any manner or respect whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that you're concerned about this, Mr. Guy-Smith. At the same time, on the basis of the earlier answers of the witness, I did not find anything specific in this question which would be inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate the Chamber's present ruling. I'm asking for the utmost caution at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney, I think you will have understood that Mr. Guy-Smith is insisting more than usual on the questions being put to the witness in the appropriate way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note my colleague's concern and I will ask the question again of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you were shown these photographs, were you with your brother or were you alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was with my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where did this happen? Where in Pristina were you when you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask first for another -- you said you were with your brother. Was the photo-array shown to you alone or was it shown to you and your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That day, when we went together, my brother was sitting a bit away from me and they showed this photo-array only to me, asking me whether I recognised anyone there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you were shown this photo-array and asked if you recognised anyone inside of it, did you? Did you recognise anyone in the photo-array?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Who did you recognise inside the photo-array?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised in that photo-array the Togeri.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After you recognised the photo of Togeri, did you do anything to the photo-array to note that recognition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drew a circle around the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would like to show the witness, under seal, please, the 65 ter Exhibit 711.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, can you see that image on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was this the photo-array that was shown to you by the investigator that you've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise any marks in your writing on that exhibit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Please point those out to us. What do you recognise on that exhibit that is in your writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Below the number 6 in this exhibit appears to be some writing. Do you recognise that writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Without telling us what is written there, without telling us the words that are written there, what did you write in that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What do you want of me, to tell you what it is written there or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. Tell us what is written there but don't say the words out loud. Just tell us generally what you put in that location under the number 6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my name and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Also around the number 6 in this exhibit, there's a -- appears to be a hand-drawn mark; is that correct, Witness 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking of number 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And do you recognise that hand-drawn mark around the number 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you make that mark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In the right-hand upper portion of this exhibit is more handwriting which appears to be a date. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's not me who has written that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the date that is written there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm certainly going to object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I can ask that question in a different way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kearney. Yes, then please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, do you remember the date that you were shown this photo-array?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but I know that we went there to look at these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All right. Also during the course of the investigation, did you provide a sample of your DNA to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Sometime after supplying a sample of your DNA to the investigators, did you receive back remains of any of your family members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the bodies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After they took the blood samples, which was after they asked if we would allow them to exhume the bodies, then we said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you ever receive back after that time period, after the exhumation, after the DNA samples, did you ever receive back for burial any members of your family that had been taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Which family members did you receive back for burial?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think this is a matter for -- if the witness could take off his headphones for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take off your headphones for a second, Witness 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney is asking this gentleman a question that is outside the purview of his knowledge. Representations may be made to him -- may have been made to him concerning what remains were received back by the family, but he right now is asking him a question which is so far outside his knowledge, which deals with matters of technical and scientific expertise, I think it's totally inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely. I'll see if I can make my point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say it's outside of his knowledge. The question was whether they received back any members of the family. Why would that be out of -- it's not whether the family received back, that's at least how I understood it. How couldn't he know whether he received back any bodies of members of his family?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, in this case one of the issues that will become quite clear as time goes on is certain bodies that were identified were identified incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, but let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Therefore, first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, of course, what we're asking the witness is what he knows and he may make a mistake; that's another matter. But it's not a question which, by itself, would be outside the knowledge of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If the question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If he makes a mistake, then of course that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If the question was asked -- I apologise for speaking too quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If the question was asked, Did you receive bodies that you were told were or you understood to be from information you received were, that would be a different matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then you're anticipating on your knowledge of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could ask the witness what was the source of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Rather than beat a dead horse, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness can put his earphones on again. And you may put the questions to the witness, and you are aware, Mr. Kearney, that Mr. Guy-Smith has some concerns about the source of knowledge and of the quality of these sources. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, after the exhumation, after your provision of a DNA sample to the ICTY, were you given, by ICTY investigators, bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And whose bodies were they that were -- whose bodies -- strike that? Did the ICTY identify whose bodies were being given back to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Who was it they told you was being given back to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the body of my sister that was taken for examination -- forensic examination (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Lastly, this gentleman that you've identified in the photograph as number 6, is he the person that you've identified throughout the course of your testimony in this case as Toger, or Togeri?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: We would tender in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But first we need to assign a number, but Madam Registrar is ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number P27, marked for identification and under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the photo-array. Yes. You'd --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you wanted to tender into evidence all the exhibits you've shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any -- since there are no objections, I think it's P25, 26, and 27, that are admitted into evidence. I am looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Might I suggest we break now and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll break now and then start cross-examination after the break. Will you be the first one to cross-examine the witness, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that I will. I've now just been -- I've just been given the nod that I shall be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps before we excuse the witness for the break, I would have one or two questions for the witness. Witness 4, you said your brother was present when the photo-array was shown to you. Could you tell us, was it at the beginning, in the middle, at the end? When was the photo-array shown to you during the course of the interview you gave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said your brother was present. Were questions put to you and to your brother at the same time, or was he just present when you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They asked the questions on the same day. They took in my brother; I don't know what he told them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get things as clear as possible. When your brother was present when the photo-array was shown to you, did he remain in that same room with you during the whole of the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For how long did he stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're referring to my brother?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we gave our statements, we gave them separately; we didn't give the statements together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you say that he was present when the photo-array was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to that day when we went there together, because on another day I went alone to give the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You told us that your brother was at some distance when the photo-array was shown to you. Could you tell us exactly how far away he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps 4 or 5 metres, in the other room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "in the other room." Do I have to understand that he was not in the same room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So did I then correctly understand you when you said He was with me, that you were referring to your brother as being in the same building but not in the same room, or how do I have to understand your testimony in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said is that he was in the same building with me but not in the same room when I was giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just find the exact location. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe it's page 21, line 14, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. A question was put to you by Mr. Kearney who asked you: "When you were shown these photographs, were you with your brother or were you alone?" You then answered: "I was with my brother."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you, in order to avoid any misunderstanding, explain exactly what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I meant is that the day when they showed the photographs to me, we went together to that place with my brother, but my brother was not present in the room where I was being interviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't interview us at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, before I put the next -- no, I'll first put the next question to you, but I would like you to wait before giving an answer. Did you speak with your brother about the interview and what you stated at this interview? And that's my question and I add immediately to that: Where I yesterday instructed you not to speak with anyone about your testimony and, therefore, you are not allowed to do that these days when you're in The Hague, that there is not a similar prohibition, at least not at the time in October 2004, there is not a similar prohibition to speak with other persons about what you stated during these interviews. So I now repeat my question: Did you speak with your brother about the interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told him that I was there to give a statement, but I didn't discuss the contents of my statement. I spoke of things that I saw in my statement, and he spoke of things that he saw in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you tell him about the photo-array that was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I have told him that I recognised the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did your brother tell you whether a photo-array was shown to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did he say? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said that he could not recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. We -- first of all, I'd like to ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, could I ask, there has been made a submission for further protective measures in relation to Witness 49? Could the Chamber hear from the Defence when it intends, if at all, to respond to that submission?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we have to go into private session, do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not at all. I think the application is for closed testimony altogether. Would Your Honours permit us to respond to that tomorrow morning? And may we do so orally, or would Your Honours request a response in writing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I said tomorrow morning. Obviously, if I'm responding orally, it would be at the beginning of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the beginning. Yes, that's fine. At the same time, Mr. Kearney or Mr. Di Fazio, just for argument's sake, if there would be any problem with closed session, do you expect that you will elicit from the witness any testimony that we should hear in private session because that could identify the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would you please consider, because we would then further hear from the Defence tomorrow to what extent private session would serve the purposes and to what extent closed session is really necessary, and also in view -- against the background of the reasons given. We will adjourn until five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, are you ready to cross-examine Witness 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Witness 4, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Guy-Smith, who is counsel for the Defence, for at least one of the Defence, Mr. Balaj. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take it that we are presently in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for one brief moment?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You've told us that a gentleman by the name of Slobodan Prascevic came to your home on occasion; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us how you communicated with Slobodan Prascevic? And by that I mean, did you call him on a telephone, on a radio? How did he know when to come to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you referring to? Is it about the day when there was firing or about any other day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: For the moment I'm speaking about, generally speaking, how your family was able to get hold of this particular individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, at that time we didn't have a phone, but he also didn't come that often to visit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you have a radio by which you could communicate with this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you received information that he was dead, you've told us that you received that information from the radio; true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I meant a radio, not a radio for communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And was that a radio that you had at your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that day when we heard about this we were not at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say where I was but I don't want the others to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Very well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In that case, could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you went to the village that we've just mentioned, before you went to that village you would obtain permission to go there; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You would obtain that permission, as you've called it, the headquarters of the KLA which you've identified as a grocery shop which belonged, I believe, to Zef Avdyli. Isn't that what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And on the occasions that you went to get authorisation to travel away from your home, you went by yourself, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did your brother ever go to get authorisation to travel at Zef Avdyli's shop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know. I really have nothing to say about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: Apart from yourself for purposes of travelling, do you recall during the summer months your brother travelling away from the family home, in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember once he did leave the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you say that he left the house, to your knowledge, did he leave the house and go to another village which required him to receive authorisation to travel on that one occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did he travel by himself or did he travel with somebody else in the family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he travelled by himself. As far as the authorisation is concerned, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You've told us that on a number of different occasions your home was visited by individuals wearing black clothes; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The very first time that happened and men came to your home wearing black clothes, these were men that you knew, were they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For the first time I didn't know them, but during the second or the third time I recognised them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, the very first time that men came to visit your home wearing black clothes, those men were, among others, Mr. Rexhepi, Mr. Islami, and Mr. Zefi, were they not? People who you've known for years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't say that Islami and the others were wearing black clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The very first time men came to your home, you said that three or four men came inside and they were wearing black masks. And now with regard to the issue of clothes, you said some were wearing civilian clothes, if I'm not mistaken, some were wearing military clothes. I've identified for the moment three men; that would be Mr. Rexhepi, Mr. Islami and Mr. Zefi. With regard to Mr. Rexhepi, was he wearing black clothes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this question appears to be severely compound. There's several sentences worth of information in it. I would ask my esteemed colleague that if he wants to refer to a portion of this witness's past testimony, that he actually read that testimony back to the witness for the sake of clarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, compound questions usually lead to confusion rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no desire to confuse anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed with this in your mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During the first visit to your home --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could please quote the line on the transcript, then we'll all give -- give such words that we are able to find it, so that we can better follow your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm coming to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Tell us about this group of masked men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, they came with masks and painted in their faces, and I didn't recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you say that you did not recognise them, are you telling us that three to four men that came to your home on that day, you did not recognise any of those men as being the gentlemen that I've just mentioned to you: Mr. Rexhepi, Mr. Islami, or Mr. Zefi.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came another day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I appreciate that you say they came another day. But the first time, you didn't recognize any of those three men as being the ones who came to your home; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't recognise them because that was the first time they came.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The next time that men came to your home, wearing black, you were asleep and it was in the night-time; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you woke up, you woke up because you heard a noise inside your home; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You did not see the car in which these men arrived, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And during the second time that men in black came to your home, if I understood your testimony correctly, you were behind a door which was being guarded; true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your home had no electricity; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: While you were behind the door that was being guarded, you've told us that your mother was having conversation with one or more of the men dressed in black; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that part of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you say "that part of the house," you mean in a part of the house away from where you were behind the door that was being guarded; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, you are using the word "behind" now, I think, three or four times. Could you just guide us to where I find in the testimony of the witness that he said that he was behind that door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm asking the witness of whether that's correct, whether he's behind a door? If he says he's behind a door --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you said whether -- let me just check what you exactly said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On page 40, line 1, my question is: "And during the second time that the men in black came to your home, if I understood your testimony correctly, you were behind a door ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me do this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's also a very compound question, but -- so let's take it one by one instead of -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After you were -- after you were woken up the second time that the men in black came to your home, you stayed in your bedroom behind a door that was being guarded; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not behind the door. I didn't say behind the door; I said in the bedroom, when they came and woke us up. I said that that person stood guard there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How far away was the conversation that your mother was having with the men in black while you were in the bedroom being guarded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably 4 or 5 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You've told us that during that conversation you heard a name being repeatedly said; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Apart from the name that you've told us you heard us repeatedly being mentioned, what else did you hear in that conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the name mentioned by someone else and then he was talking with my mother in that other part of the house, 4 or 5 metres away. When we awoke in the morning, mum told us what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The information that you received and how you learned what happened that night was information you received from your mother the next day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Objection; vague. Information is a very general term. I would ask that the witness be asked specifics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness to take his earphones off for a second?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before we do that, Your Honour, may I inquire whether or not the witness speaks English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you put them on? Do you understand any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Very, very little, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please take off your earphones? Mr. Guy-Smith, many of your questions are creating quite some confusion. For example, if you say -- there are a lot of implicit suggestions in your questions which might easily not be picked up, understood, by a witness, and then of course, the answers he gives are not easy to evaluate. Let me just give you a few examples. For example, one of your earlier questions, you suggested that the person you talked about would come to the house only when called, where there's nothing in the evidence until that moment that would suggest it, as far as I understand. One of your next questions, luckily, the witness picked it up that where you were talking about radio, it was very ambiguous, your question. And now in one of your last questions, you more or less suggested - and let me try to find your exact words before I continue - you said: "Apart from the name that you've told us you heard as repeatedly being mentioned, what else did you hear in that conversation?" Which strongly suggests that the mentioning of the name was part of the conversation, whereas the witness clearly testified earlier that he heard the other men using the name and that he was informed by his mother the next morning. So by these implicit suggestions in your question, you create confusion which does not assist the Chamber. Please keep this in mind. We'll ask the witness to put his earphones on again and we'll continue. Witness. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The second visit you were not able to personally identify Toger as being there that evening, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Three or four days after the second visit in the evening, your sister S came back home; true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At the time that she came home, she came home in a white car; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Where were you when you first saw your sister come home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the vicinity of the house, or to say -- to be more exact, in the courtyard of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You've told us there was another person with your sister who was in the car; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That person was wearing black; true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your sister came in the home and stayed for, I think, approximately 30 to 40 minutes; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The person who came with her in the car, dressed in black, stayed in the car during the period of time your sister was visiting for 30 to 40 minutes; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: To be exact, can you confirm having seen him all these 30 to 40 minutes in the car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He came -- first, he came out of the car together with my sister. He didn't stay long outside. And then I saw him get into the car. Then I went home -- I entered the house with my sister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you entered the home with your sister, following up on the Judge's question, did you keep an eye out on the car for the 30 to 40 minutes that you were visiting with your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was inside the house, I didn't go out to see what was happening with the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: While you were inside the house, did you look outside at the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. We were sitting in another room from which you couldn't see the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: On the second visit with sister S, you said that she came in a car; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When she came in the car the second time, did she come alone or did she come at that time with a man dressed in black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And I take it when you say "yes," you mean that she came that time with a man dressed in black; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Was anybody else in the car except for your sister and this man dressed in black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When she was brought to the house, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you saw her being brought to the house on her second visit in the morning with the man who was dressed in black, after she came to the area of your home, she got out of the car; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The car left; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And then you spent some hours with your sister; true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: There came a time in the afternoon when your sister told you that it was time to leave; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When she told you it was time to leave, you decided to walk with her back --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, the only two people who left the house at that point in time in the afternoon were yourself and your sister; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: About how long a period of time were you walking before you got to the - I think it's called - the ford, or Ratis ford?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I remember, it was for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what direction were you walking in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After you had been walking for about 25 minutes, you came to an area where there was a river or a stream; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And at that point in time, your sister told you - it was about halfway - your sister told you that you didn't need to come with her any further; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: She went forward towards --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And you returned home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that it took you about as long to get back home from the ford as it took you to go from the house to the ford? And by that, I mean it took you about 25 minutes, walking, to get home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was the same amount of time. Maybe it was shorter. But it was something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you got home, you were home for a short period of time when a car came to the house again; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: There were a number of men in black in that car; true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only the person who came during -- every time, while the others, I didn't recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
