utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, because your answer is: "No. Only the person who came during -- every time, while the others, I didn't recognise them." When you returned home and the car came, was there one person in the car or more than one person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Very well. Both of those people were wearing black; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see what the other person was wearing, and I spoke to them from a distance of 7 or 8 metres. I do not remember what the other person was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And after you spoke to them from a distance of 7 or 8 metres, they left; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The next time that you had any contact with any individuals wearing black was two or three weeks after you had left your sister at the ford; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but what are you referring to? What location?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At your home, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they came, it was two or three weeks later. At this time, some persons came to our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And you've told us that that was around the harvesting of the corn when that occurred; true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was during autumn because you do this in the field during the autumn, twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, you've corrected me on something that I don't know. So it was sometime in the autumn after the corn had been harvested one time, I guess, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First you do the harvest of the beans in autumn and then the last is the corn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When that visit occurred, the visit that occurred in the autumn, you've told us that a number of men in black came and, I believe, had a conversation with your mother; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, the conversation that you've told us about, which was, I believe - and I'm referring the Court and counsel to page 87, begins on the bottom of page 86 - "they talked to the mother" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're using, then, numbers which continue, so not just the numbering of the day, and if you would give us some text, then -- a word which doesn't appear on every line, then we'll easily find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "They talked to the mother ..." I believe it's 1445, at line 4, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I hope that was of some help. "They talked to the mother, and did you hear that conversation?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And that is a conversation that you overheard; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And that is a conversation that concerned the issue of whether or not people could leave the home with or without authorisation; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they came for the second time after my sister went missing,

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: told us, I believe, that the person who had that conversation with your mother was somebody you have identified as Toger; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, that particular piece of information, that the person who had the conversation with your mother was Toger, that's information that you spoke to Mr. Kearney about before you came to testify here, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And you told Mr. Kearney, did you not, that you heard a KLA soldier tell your mother that everyone could get travel documents except her, and that if she tried to leave she'd be killed; right? That's what you told Mr. Kearney?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours and counsel, my colleague -- my dear colleague, I would simply ask that if there is a reference made to a prior statement or proofing notes, that my colleague direct the Court and counsel to the specific area where it is so we can all follow along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's 2D21-317, page 2 of the proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you've just told us that you told Mr. Kearney that the person who had this conversation with your mother was Toger; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that what you told Mr. Kearney was that the person who had this conversation with your mother was a person whose name was Aslan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Trial Chamber, I'm sorry to interrupt again. Counsel, are you referring to page 2 of the proofing notes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I also tried to find that but -- could you give us how that paragraph starts so that we could more easily find it, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "Visits to KLA HQ in Ratis."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's -- for me it's the first page of the proofing notes, but--

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "The witness confirms" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can read it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And then it would be the second -- it would be the third full sentence, "The witness adds ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll read it. Yes, I've got it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to get an answer to my last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please repeat the question, but let me just read another matter for one second. Yes. Again, could the witness take his earphones off for another second? Mr. Guy-Smith, you were talking about a conversation the mother had with a person identified by the witness. You said: "I believe that the person who had that conversation with your mother was somebody you had identified as Toger; correct?" Yes. Now, that particular piece of information you said, that the person who had a conversation with your mother was Toger, that's information that you spoke to Mr. Kearney about before, and then you said: "And you told Mr. Kearney, did you not, that you heard a KLA soldier tell your mother and everyone, and who it was?" Do I understand you well that you -- yes, you said: "Now, you've just told us that you told to Mr. Kearney that the person who had this conversation with your mother was Toger; right?" Let me just see. I'm just trying to ... Where did the witness say exactly that he told that it was Toger who gave that information? Because you're putting that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I asked him the question as to whether he did that during his proofing. That's where the question -- Did you tell Mr. Kearney that Toger was the person who threatened -- I'm rephrasing the question at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then just try to find out exactly where you put this to the witness, where exactly -- "You told Mr. Kearney that you heard a KLA told to your mother that everyone ..." Then the next question was guided: "Now, you've just told us that you told Mr. Kearney that the person who had this conversation with your mother was Toger." Where did he say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm asking him whether he said that to Mr. Kearney. It's not -- this is a question I asked him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you're saying -- "now you've just told that you told Mr. Kearney that ..." Where did he say that? I'm just looking at the transcript, where he said that he told to Mr. Kearney that it was Toger who gave that information?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe it's there. I'm not going to go up to it. I'll go through this again for the purposes of the Court's clarification; shall I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you spoke to Mr. Kearney before you came to testify in court, you told Mr. Kearney that Toger was the one who threatened your mother; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Again, vague is the time now, Your Honour. Perhaps we can just read the quote from the proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, we're not reading the quote from the proofing notes because that's not the purpose of what we're doing here. When you spoke to Mr. Kearney during --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Guy-Smith, let me just intervene at this moment. You put to the witness earlier that he just told you that it was Toger -- let me just give you the line and the -- page 50, line 5; yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have to get up to mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Now, you've told us ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Hold on, hold on. I'm now with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. "Now, you've just told us that you told Mr. Kearney that the person who had this conversation with your mother was Toger; right?" The answer is yes. And I think that the witness testified that there was a conversation with Toger. Next question: "Well, isn't it true --"

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, Your Honour, if you would take a look at the previous page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Give me the line?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be line 8: "The information with (redacted), I believe, that the person who had that conversation with your mother was somebody you identified as Toger; correct?" Answer: "Yes, yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "Now, that particular piece of information, that the person who had the conversation with your mother was Toger, that's information that you spoke to Mr. Kearney about before you came to testify here, did you not?" Answer: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not quarrel with that. However, that is separate from the threats that we're talking about now. When she was taken away is different than when she was threatened not to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I find it all rather confusing, as a matter of fact. We have -- we're talking about threats, we're talking about permits to travel, and we're talking about conversations, and it's not always clearly distinguished with whom exactly what subject was discussed. And in order to put it to the witness, or at least to invite the witness to think about whether he has been inconsistent in this respect, we need greatest precision. You may proceed on this basis, Mr. -- and the Chamber would prefer that you read to the witness what he said on the basis of the transcript, and that you read to the witness what is reflected in the proofing notes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that's the entire difficulty with the proofing notes, because we don't know whether the proofing notes are, in fact, complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we don't know, but if you want to confront the witness with what's in the proofing notes, you should -- you should quote the proofing notes. We can't just speculate on whether there had been anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if I might refer the Court and counsel to page 49, line 5, which is discussing the self-same conversation: "And that is a conversation concerning the issue of whether or not people could leave the home with or without authorisation; right?" Answer: "When they came for the second time after my sister went missing, (redacted)" So, in fact, we're talking about the same time, the same conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, same time, yes. Same conversation is -- yes, the answer does not --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you ever tell Mr. Kearney during the time that you were proofed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I think the witness should put the headphones on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be far better for him to hear the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you ever tell Mr. Kearney during the time that you were involved in your proofing sessions on March 9th and March 12th that Togeri threatened to kill your mother if she left the home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to the headquarters to take permission because they refused to give me permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, my question is: Did you tell Mr. Kearney, the gentleman who's sitting over there. Did you tell Mr. Kearney this? And "this" means that Togeri threatened to kill your mother if she left the home, and you overheard such a conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this was said by Rexhepi, by Aslan Rexhepi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So it wasn't said by the person you called Togeri. Togeri never threatened your mother, she would be killed or he would kill her if she left the home, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that this -- I don't remember this, about her leaving the house. But I know only that he talked with mother when he

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, let's turn into private session in order to avoid that we have to make many more redactions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Before you went to Pristina in 2004 to look at the photo-spread, had you seen any television reporting concerning Idriz Balaj being tried in the Dukagjin courthouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he was being tried, I didn't see anything. But when I heard something about an accident, I saw it actually on television, the news, saying that they had fired -- they had fired at this house or thrown something at this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you saw something on television, that they had fired at his house or thrown something at his house, you learned that his name was Idriz Balaj and he was also -- had a nickname at that time, did you not? He was identified in the news as being Idriz Balaj, also Togeri?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I'd like you to split up these things clearly, so first ask whether it was Balaj, then the next question is whether a nickname was used as well, because otherwise we get confirmations on three, four, or five subjects and later find out that there might be a need to correct. I didn't want to interrupt you when the question was put to you, but you are invited to follow this guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you saw the television report concerning something being thrown at his house, you heard -- there were two names associated with that. One was the name of Idriz Balaj; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And the other name that you heard was the name of Toger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you heard the name of Toger, that name was associated with the name of Idriz Balaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That happened in 2002; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: What kind of report was that? Can you give us some details?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was an explosive thrown at his house. When he left it with his wife and his children, the explosive was blown, and this was said in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And who or what was shown in the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They showed some unidentified persons who were thought to be the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And they also showed a picture of Idriz Balaj on that news reporting; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And they showed a picture of his wife also, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the small child.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, apart from that one television reporting, did you have an opportunity to read in the newspaper anything concerning this attempt on Idriz Balaj and his family? And by that I mean this assassination attempt.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't read anything. I didn't have an opportunity to read anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: After you saw the television reporting concerning this particular matter, and by that I mean the murder attempt, did you ever see any television reporting on the Dukagjin trial where Idriz Balaj was being tried with some other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I have one final question for you, which is: Doesn't the word "Toger" mean lieutenant in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we didn't know that. We learned it later. We learned that there is a rank in the police which is called, as he was called, during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you're the next in line.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do have some questions for this witness, but you also have a matter of some urgency that needs to be raised with Your Honour before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it's unlikely that I will conclude my cross-examination and Mr. Kearney conclude any re-examination before the break, so may I raise those issues with Your Honours now, because they do need to be resolved before the break rather than after them -- after it. I'm in Your Honours' hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I've got no idea about the urgency of the matter. I hope it's not disclosure again. At the same time, would it be something that the witness, being in court, would disturb any of your -- we could -- of course, we could ask him to leave the courtroom -- how much time do you think you would need --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would have thought five --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Between five and ten minutes in total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Between five and ten minutes. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no questions. Then, yes, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: If I may be heard on this matter, my re-direct, at least to date, is exceedingly short. Just for the sake of the witness, I wonder if we could just finish with him before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest the following: I suggest that you first put your questions to the witness so that we do the cross-examination; that we'll then ask the usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom; that we'll then hear the procedural matter, and then upon return, when we have resumed, that then Mr. Kearney will re-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I should make it absolutely clear, the procedural matter does not relate to this witness but to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, therefore, if it suits Mr. Kearney, having concluded my few short questions, I have no objection to him - if he is going to be brief - re-examining before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, it depends -- I do not know who is going to take the next witness, and I also do not know whether you have to consult with anyone, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The next witness, Your Honour, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether -- I have to look on my list whether there's any protective measures in place or not, and, of course, it would not be appropriate to discuss any matter on the next witness in the presence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I would say simply that the next witness is being handled by Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, if you get in touch with Mr. Dutertre, if you would now cross-examine the witness, continue your cross-examination, and then once we are finished cross-examination, we'll -- contact will be made with Mr. Dutertre and we'll reserve your time until after the break. Witness 4, this is all not very interesting for you. Mr. Emmerson will now further cross-examine you. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just going to ask you one or two short questions on behalf of Ramush Haradinaj. First of all, you gave evidence yesterday that on the night before the incident in which the police officer was shot in his car, an incident had occurred to a family's home in Ratis and the name that you gave us was Malesha. You told us that you could not recall his surname, but that you had seen damage to the house when you went there. I just want to clarify the identity of that individual in case there should be any misunderstanding about the number of incidents of this nature that had occurred in Ratis. Does the name Nastadin Culafic mean anything to you, also known as Malesha?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The couple that you referred to at the house in Ratis, you went to see the house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why I had to go to that village, and I went and had a look at this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know the couple who lived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew only the man and his wife, but I don't remember her name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, let me see if I can jog your memory. We've heard evidence in this court already that a couple by the name of Culafic - the husband named Nastadin, also known as Malesha, and the wife named Jela, J-e-l-a - had damage to their house at about the time that you're describing. And I just want to understand whether the Malesha that you're telling us about is the same Malesha that we have already heard about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him only as Malesha, but I don't know any other name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But that is his first name and not his surname; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We always used to call him Malesha. Everybody knew him for that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you said in your evidence yesterday that apart from that one incident, you weren't aware of any other incidents of damage to Serb houses in Ratis at about that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, vague as to the time, the word "at that time." Are we talking about the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- before the Prascevic murder?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With respect, it's not at all vague. I put the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the time frame is quite clear, and I even remember that there was agreement between the parties on the 2nd of March, isn't it? So 2nd or 3rd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, this witness wasn't able to recall the date which is why I didn't put it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But what I did put him, which I hope Mr. Kearney accepts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, his own testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- is remotely vague, is that it was the night before the incident he's given evidence about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can I repeat the question, please. It's right, is it, as you told us yesterday, that apart from that one incident that occurred on the night before the shooting of the police officer, you were not aware of any other incidents of damage to Serb houses in Ratis at around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, with the exception of that house. That night I don't know of any other house that was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to turn to some other questions which relate to the night that your sister M was taken. Don't anticipate my question. I want to take it with you slowly and in stages. I want, first of all, to show you a statement that you made, and signed, to the Prosecution on the 25th of July, 2006. Just so that you understand how I'm proceeding, this statement was taken by a French lady. Do you remember being interviewed by a French-speaking interviewer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at the end of the interview, correct -- you were -- sorry, I'll put the question differently. At the end of the interview, there was an interpreter present who read the French statement to you in Albanian, who gave you the opportunity to correct the statement; that you then confirmed that the statement was accurate, and you put your signature on the French statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we had some problems with the interpreters because they could not clearly understand us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just going to read you a short passage from the end of the statement because, obviously, if you had problems with the interpretation, it's important that we get it straight. At the end of the statement is a certificate by the interpreter who says: "I have orally translated the above statement from French into Albanian in the presence of (redacted), who appears to have heard and understood my translation of this statement. (redacted)"

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Too fast?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do apologise. That was a -- that was a serious oversight on my part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apologies accepted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The certificate goes on to say that you had acknowledged that the matters set out in the statement as translated were true, to the best of your knowledge and recollection, and that accordingly you had signed your signature on the French statement where indicated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can we take it that by the time you signed the statement, you understood what it said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we please just look briefly -- I'll give the three references. The French original with the signature on -- all of these should, obviously, appear under seal or appear in closed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do I understand that we get now the French versions as exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I make it clear that I'm not going to tender this document, but if it's to be marked for identification, then I think the process is that the French version be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you'll read from the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the Albanian translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the Albanian translation. So what, then, is still missing is the link between --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was going to take it in stages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the French. Yes. I'd like to have a look at the French version at the same time when you're dealing with the English version so that I could identify if there's any problem in relation to that. Now, just how to get that on my screen. I take it if you have the right number, I can find the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can give you the number for each one. The French translation -- I'm sorry, the French original is 2D21-0468, the English translation is 2D21-0305, and the Albanian translation of the statement for the witness is 2D21-0476.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for everybody's assistance, the page numbers may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that if they have to be marked for identification, they should receive numbers. Madam Registrar, for first the French version, last four digits, 0468.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's one document and all the different versions are attached to the original, and the original, Madam Registrar, would be the French?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it's the French original, which would have the Exhibit number D13, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the passages that I want to look at -- we can look at the witness's signature, if that would assist, but I think it's common ground that this is the statement that he signed. Would it assist Your Honours to have the French translation with the signature on it shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The French original.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: French original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'd rather -- most important for me is to get the French language on my screen, rather than -- Is there any dispute about this ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll get the French version. I don't think that there's any dispute about this witness having signed these statements, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, then, we could proceed with the content rather than with the form.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so for the witness in Albanian, for those who speak English in the English version, and for Your Honour in the French as well, the two paragraphs I want to look at are paragraphs 29 and 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They may not be on identical pages, but fortunately the paragraphs are numbered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, could we enlarge paragraphs 29 and 30 for the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see on your screen, in your own language, paragraphs 29 and 30?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can you just read paragraphs 29 and 30 over to yourself. But before you do, may I make it clear that - and this is for the Judges as well as for yourself - the name that appears in paragraph 29, Rexh Islami, you have already corrected in your evidence and I think as well when you spoke to Mr. Kearney before you came to give evidence, and what it should say, I think, is Xhevat Islami. So I'm not looking to ask you about that particular difference. But could you just read paragraphs 29 and 30 to yourself, first of all, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Apart from that one error where the statement refers to Rexh Islami rather than Xhevat Islami, are those two paragraphs accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I just want to be clear because there was a translation given during your evidence-in-chief earlier this afternoon where you were referring to Xhevat Islami on the night that M was taken, and as it came across the translation to us and, therefore, on the transcript, what was translated was "Xhevat said he had come to our house in the name of Ramush Haradinaj." And then a little later on, you were asked exactly what had Xhevat said, and you said: "Xhevat said, 'I am Ramush'." And you were asked: "Did you believe him?" And you said: "No, I did not believe him because we knew who it was." Just pause there. I'm just reminding you first of the evidence that you gave earlier, and then I'm going to ask you some questions. Just to be clear, did the man you believed was Xhevat Islami, did he say, "I am Ramush" or did he say, "I am Ramush Haradinaj"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, "I am Ramush Haradinaj."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you knew immediately that it was not Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you say in your statement that this wasn't the only time you had heard this man pretending to be Ramush Haradinaj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I know for sure, that night he said, "I am Ramush."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear - again, I'm not trying to trick you in any way - you say in your statement that this was not the first time you'd heard him introduce himself that way. Now, if you can't remember now one way or the other whether you'd ever heard him do it before, then please say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for sure that that night he said that he was Ramush. It is possible that he had introduced himself with that name on other occasions, but for that I cannot assure you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this was a man, you told us, that you knew because he'd come to your house on many occasions before the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, just to be clear, the man I'm referring to in that question is Xhevat Islami, so let me put it again. Xhevat Islami had come to your house on many occasions before the war, and that was how you were able to recognise him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you can confirm that even on the occasion that we're talking about, when M was taken, he was not the man in charge, as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Turning to paragraph 30, you say: "I've never seen Ramush Haradinaj in person ..." Can I ask you this: Does it follow from that that during the time you were in Ratis, you never saw Ramush Haradinaj in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never seen him in the area of Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you had heard that he was a good soldier and a good commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You had heard that he had lived abroad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that time no, but I heard about this later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, you later heard that he had previously lived abroad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you had never heard him described as a killer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard anyone say that he had killed someone or that he had imprisoned someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. Emmerson? Mr. Harvey, the situation as it was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: As it was before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: If I could be heard, I have a very brief question about this statement and I'll be done, we can finish with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's just one question, then I suggest that -- although I scheduled on the basis of five to ten minutes from Mr. Emmerson, which was a bit more, but if it's just one question, then let's proceed. Mr. Kearney will -- Mr. Kearney will put another question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 4, I want to direct your attention to that same paragraph that you were just asked about. This is paragraph 29 in your 2006 statement. This is before you on the screen in Albanian, I believe. I want to read the last sentence in that paragraph to you and I'm going to ask you to comment on that, please. It reads: "In spite of everything, it was Toger who seemed to be the head of the operation." Now, this is the operation, I believe, you're referring to during which sister M was taken? I want to ask you, first of all, does that accurately reflect what you told the investigator in 2006; namely, that Toger seemed to be the head of that operation? Did you tell the investigator that, the French investigator, in 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that I told her that on every occasion when they came Toger was the number one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you told her that, did you believe -- or was that the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you told the investigator that Toger seemed to be the person in charge on every occasion, was that the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to what I said, to my words?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/04 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 4, since I do not see any further request for additional questions by Defence counsel and since the Chamber has no further questions for you, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague, and to have answered questions of both parties and of the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, could you please escort Witness 4 out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time. I'm conscious of the need to ensure that the staff have an appropriate rest period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Dutertre has arrived in court. I'm going, with Your Honour's leave, to make an effort to see if this matter can be clarified and resolved for certainty without having to trouble Your Honours, and therefore may I invite you to return after the break and then, if need be, we will seek your assistance in respect of this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The disadvantage of that approach is that we cannot use the 20 minutes we have available to think about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just introduce --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you just indicate what the matter is and then we'll wait and see whether you resolve it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can indicate the problem. Just before we resumed after the last break, Mr. Di Fazio provided me with the bundle in my left hand of Rule 68 material relevant to the next witness and the witness to follow. Can I indicate in a sentence: The content of this material includes -- it may be better if, just for a second, we go into closed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, is there any Defence exhibits still to be admitted or not admitted? I think we dealt with the Prosecution exhibits but not yet with the Defence exhibits which, if tendered, would have to be tendered under seal anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not tendering this witness's statement. His testimony covered the issue quite adequately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So do we leave them then marked for identification? Because the witness was invited to read paragraphs 29 and 30, and it should be on the record somewhere what he read, actually, because it was not literally read to him after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's not tendered. It remains, then, marked for identification. I just have to go through the technicalities with Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there are a few admission decisions still pending, P22, et cetera, we'll deal with that first thing tomorrow. Mr. Dutertre, are you ready to call your next witness? I do understand the next witness is without protective measures, and that witness would be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I am ready. It's Miloica Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I understand you to be Mr. Vlahovic. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vlahovic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Dutertre, who's counsel for the Prosecution. We're in open session. [Interpretation] Mr. Dutertre, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your name is Miloica Vlahovic. You were born on July 12, 1965 in Pec, in Kosovo. Your nationality is -- your ethnic origin in Serb. You were a teacher from 1989 to 1999 in Decane, and until June 12, 1999, you lived in Kosovo. Is all this true?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Your family home was located in Gornji Ratis. I apologise for the pronunciation. This is where your father Milovan and your mother Milka Vlahovic lived, and you also lived there off and on. By this, I mean that you would spend some time there, but you also had another home in Djakovica, a house that belonged to you, with a restaurant that also belonged to you. Is all this true?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, you were a teacher in Decani. What pupils did you have? Was this school open to all? I mean, was it open to Serbs as well as people -- Albanians?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was open to both.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: The pupils in this school, could you tell us what ethnic origin they were?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They were Albanian, Roma, and Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: As a majority, Albanian families were sending their children to the school, or did they have their own schools that they sent their children to?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Up until 1991, they used to send their children to that school. Later on, they continued to send their children to state schools in ethnically clean households. They just continued to send their children to the state schools in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Why was there this change in 1991? And why was there this will to send their children to schools that they would control themselves?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from 1991 on, they were no longer willing to accept the curriculum of the Serbian state ministry. They wanted to follow their own curriculum, the one that was planned in Albania, and that's why the ethnic Albanians no longer wanted to send their children to environments where they were in touch with Serbs. In Decani municipality, the Serbs were in the centre. As for the other schools, those in the provinces, in the surrounding areas, they would send their children to state schools.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What was the ethnic make-up between Serbs, Albanians, and Romas, in your family village of Gornji Ratis in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: There were few Serbs, perhaps about 20, up to 30. All the rest were Albanians. There were no Roma people in Ratishe.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please move closer to the microphone? We can't hear him. Also, one of the microphones is off; could that be switched on, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the ethnic composition between Serbs, Albanians, and Romas, in the ten years before that?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Normally, most of the Serbs moved during the 1960s, but in my village, the village of Ratishe, there was an elementary school there. When I was a student there, for example, back in 1974 -- or, rather, throughout the 1970s, there were about 20 students there. In 1980, when my youngest brother finished school, there were just two Serb students, and in that way you could tell how many Serbs had left. There were hardly any Serbs left. The elementary school in Gornji Ratis was also used by people in Gornji Ratis, but it had no more Serb students after 1980. Not a single Serb student was left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Why did the Serb population leave Gornji Ratis? Could you tell us the reasons?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I can. There were several reasons. The ethnic Albanians, the Siptars, pressured people. They raped girls. Not in Ratishe but elsewhere. There was no freedom of movement for them. They would inflict large-scale damage on the cornfields. They would set fire to people's haystacks and livestock in villages in the area. Also, they did not allow the Serbs to use the public irrigation system, which is what people used for their cornfields and for all sorts of vegetables that they grew. The Serbs were not allowed access to this public irrigation system.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When did you know that the situation was actually deteriorating in the relationship between Serbs and Albanians?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The situation was always tense; you must know that. But particularly 1990 and 1991 when there were cases of poisoning in schools and they refused to study the Serbian language, I was still teaching at Gramocelj, teaching the Serbian language to Albanian kids, between 1989 and 1991 -- September 1991. That's when the tensions really began to mount.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: To be more specific, in 1997 and 1998, how did the situation evolve?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you say that you were teaching Albanian language to Serbian kids?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was teaching the Serbian language to Albanian kids.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In 1997, at the end of 1997 and in 1998, how would you describe the situation prevailing between the Serb population and the Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Late in 1997 and early 1998, the situation at the village of Rznic and Prilep and Ratishe, and that was on the way from Gornji Ratis travelling from Djakovica, people in camouflage would turn up. They were armed. They would stop cars of Serbs and Albanians alike. They IDed people. They let some people go; they held some people back. And in 1998, Ratishe Borizan [phoen], a village called Glodjane, the distance being about 1 or 2 kilometres as the crow flies. There was a training camp there. You could hear sounds of shooting often in the afternoon, shooting -- sounds of shooting coming from automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned armed men wearing camouflage uniform and stopping cars. Who were these men? What was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And how did you know this yourself? Who told you, or what was your personal experience of these events?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No one ever pulled me over, although I used to travel quite a bit. Maybe I was just lucky. The Stojanovic brothers were pulled over as they were travelling. They lived near the village of Glodjane, very close to the village of Glodjane. I also heard from some ethnic Albanians, that's the sort of thing that people were saying at the time, that they were pulling people over.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, let's talk about the brothers Stojanovic for a second. Could we have their first names, please, and could you tell us exactly what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Before the witness answers, could Mr. Dutertre establish the basis of the witness' knowledge before he asks him to give testimony as to what happened to these individuals, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, yes. I was going to get there in my next question, but I could ask it right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How do you know what happened to the Stojanovic brothers, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When did they tell you, and on which occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They told me that in 1998, April, I think it was the end of April. I don't know the exact date. The man who had been beaten up, Dragoslav Stojanovic, was in hospital in Pristina, whereas his brother Mijat Stojanovic sustained only some injuries and didn't have to go to the hospital. And also with them was their cousin Stijovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: These three individuals --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the full name of the last person he mentioned, the cousin, you said. What's the full name of the cousin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Veselin Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least I interpreted "counsel" as "cousin." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he's a cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The French translation was precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm switching from French to English and it sometimes disallows me to hear exactly what was said, so therefore if the transcript is wrong, I don't know whether it's a translation error or whether it's a transcribing error. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Witness, did these three individuals tell what happened, or was it just one of them or two of them?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: On that specific occasion, I talked to Dragoslav Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What did he tell you exactly about the individual who stopped them and what had happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They used to live in the village of Dubrava, that is, below the village of Glodjane. They are very close to one another. On their way home, having gone to fetch some fodder, the Albanians stopped them and detained them, and they also beat them up, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where did they detain them? Where, exactly?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They, I guess, took them to their house where they locked them up and beat them, and they also took them to the village of Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, could you make sure how the witness knows, as he argued, "I don't know," "I guess" and so on. Maybe it's just the style of his language or maybe he means it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, you said, I guess they were taken to their home and they were beaten and they were also taken to the village of Glodjane. Is that something that Dragoslav Stojanovic told you?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he told me that they first took them to their home and then later took them to the village of Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what I wanted to know was whether it was Stojanovic Dragoslav who told you this.

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was Dragoslav Stojanovic who told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, who is the Culafic family?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Malesha Culafic, although his real name is Kostadin, and his wife Jela Culafic used to live in Donji Ratis. Malesha, or, rather, both of them were people of advanced age. Malesha died three years ago and Jela is still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How old were these two people, if you know, of course?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Sixty-eight or 70. I think Jela was 68 and Malesha was around 70 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In 1998, that is?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You indicated that they lived in Donji Ratis. How far is Donji Ratis, where you yourself lived, and Gornji Ratis?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They are adjacent to each other, and maybe there was about 1.5 kilometres between our house and their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you know this couple personally?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened to them in 1998? However, before you do so, I would like to know how you heard about what happened to them, if anything at all happened to this couple. Did they tell you themselves or did you get the information from other sources?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998, I think it was February or maybe March, I'm not quite sure, I think it was late February and/or early March, their house was shelled, and I heard that from Malesha himself and from Jela as well. We were giving a memorial service for my uncle, the 40-day memorial service, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You said that their house was shelled. Did you see this house, and do you know what kind of weapon was used to shell the house?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see the house. Actually, I saw it before, but I didn't see it after the shelling. I heard that it had been hit from a hand-held launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were you told by the Culafic couple?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When did they talk to you about this incident?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in early April, between the 5th and the 10th of April, when we were giving this 40-day memorial service. This is one of our customs. And we organised it in the school building, for my uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were Mr. and Mrs. Culafic home when their house came under attack?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were, but they were in another room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, who is Slobodan Prascevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Prascevic was a police officer, or a police station commander, in Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How old was he in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but he was retired at the time. He wasn't working. He just received a decision on retirement. I think he was around 55 because the police had an accelerated pension scheme.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about what happened to him? But before you answer this question, I'd like to ask you who told you what may have happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Pavle Djukic told me about him. He lives in Gornji Ratis, near the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what did Pavle Djukic tell you exactly?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He told me that Slobo was driving a woman - I don't know her name - and her son. He was attacked and that is when he was killed, near the church in Gornji Ratis. He heard gun-shots, and this woman, I think her first name was (redacted), was also injured; whereas her son went unscathed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Djukic tell you when approximately this incident took place?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I think it also happened sometime in early April or late March.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When did he tell you about this incident himself?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He told me that around the 15th of April; that is to say, some ten days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, do you remember other incidents taking place in Donji Ratis?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The only incident I know that took place in Donji Ratis was the shelling of the church. I'm not sure whether that happened before Prascevic's murder and this other incident. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Who told you about this incident; i.e., the shelling of the church in Donji Ratis?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Dimitrije Radovic told me that. His house was next to the church. And since it was unsafe, he kept the keys to the church. The priest had given him the key for safekeeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You've just referred to the priest. Was it an Orthodox church?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Orthodox church. It belongs to the monastery of Decani, and it's the Holy Trinity Church.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to move to another subject. Where did your sister live in February 1998, and what was her name, if you only have one sister?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I have two sisters. One used to live in Pec; her name is Nada Vlahovic. And the younger sister, Natalia lived in the village of Crmljane, Djakovica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: About the latter, what happened to your sister's house in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: It was in late February, I think, or beginning of March. She was married to the Babovic family in that village. So in late February or early March, she gave birth to a child on the 16th of February, 1988 [as interpreted]. So about two weeks later, they were attacked. There were three Babovic brothers, and all three households were attacked from automatic weapons because casings were retrieved on the spot, and there were bullet-holes in the walls of the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Who told you about this incident?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: My sister told me that, and I went to see her and I saw it with my own eyes. I saw these bullet-holes and I saw the casings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did your sister tell you how many men had attacked the houses?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They said there were several attackers and that fire shot -- gun-shots came from different directions. They didn't mention any specific numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Was she able to provide a description of these men who attacked the houses?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, she couldn't describe them. They were just lying on the floor -- she was lying on the floor with her little baby, so she couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were other houses attacked on that occasion in that village?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: There are only three Serbian houses in total in the village of Crmljane, three or four maybe at the most, but the three families were living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Only those houses came under attack, then?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether the others were attacked, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Now, one question that relates to translation maybe or the way the name the village -- the name of the village should be pronounced.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the transcript, the name doesn't seem to reflect correctly the name of the village as I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat very clearly, Mr. Vlahovic, the name of the village where your sister used to live?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Crmljane, that was the name of the village. They used to call it Muva but I know that its name was Crmljane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, when did you see your father and your mother, Milovan and Milka Vlahovic, for the last time?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I saw my father and mother for the last time on the Tuesday, the 21st of April, 1988 -- 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I saw them in my house in Gornji Ratis; that's where I spent the night on the 20th of April. After spending the night, I left on the 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was the state of mind of the Serbs living in Gornji Ratis at that time, on the 21st or around this date, if there were still Serbs there?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of April there were very few people. They went to Decani and they would come back to feed the cattle. However, those who stayed were Milos Radunovic, his wife Milica; Slobo Radosevic; two Vujosevic women. One was Vukosava and the other one was called Darinka Vujosevic-Kovac. That's her husband's last name. Marka Markovic, Milojka, and her two sons were staying in Dasinovac; and also Radun Dabetic and his wife and two children stayed in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: This village being Gornji Ratis?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No. They were not all from Gornji Ratis. Some were from Dasinovac village, but this is an adjacent village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Why did the other Serbs leave and why did they only come back to feed the cattle?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Because of what happened to Malesha Culafic and what happened with the church. They felt unsafe. One could hear shooting in Glodjane, and later when I came back on the 20th, my father told me that they had been firing close to our house. They did actually fire into the air but it was very near our house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dutertre, it is almost 7.00. Could you please find an appropriate moment to conclude for today?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very briefly, a few questions and then I'll close for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, I'd like to go back to your last answer very briefly. You said that they were shooting in the air close to your house. Who was shooting in the air close to the house?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The Albanians. Among them were our neighbours from Ratis as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Is that something you saw yourself, or heard yourself, rather?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, because I wasn't home at the time. That's what my father told me on the Monday when I came back, and this happened on the Sunday before that. I had been to Sremska Kamenica with my mother to visit my later -- late uncle who was in hospital there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what were you told exactly by your father about these men? Did he provide a description of them?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask him that. I didn't see any reason why I should do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You said that shooting could be heard in Glodjane, and in one of your previous answers you said, I believe but I could be corrected if I'm wrong, I could check again, but I believe you said that it was a shooting place of sorts. How did you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could check. I could check, if you want. I could check.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Dutertre is wrong, and since it needs checking, perhaps it could be checked overnight. That's not the answer the witness gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, I could check tonight and I could ask this question tomorrow morning. The question will be more accurate. That would be in everyone's interests and I could close for the evening now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be the afternoon as we're sitting tomorrow in the afternoon. Witness, we will adjourn for the day and we'll continue tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00 in courtroom I. I instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given until now and you are still about to give tomorrow. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st day of March, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
